verdicts.reason: FeatureFlagKey.ts has 19 values. PUBLIC_FEATURE_FLAGS contains only IS_JUNCTION_RELATIONS_ENABLED; its cloud-only spread is empty. The cited usage sites gate the sub-features named (prebuilt execution mode, execution quota, conversation attach tool, validation rules, log console). No flag switches AI, MCP or apps on or off as a whole.

I re-ran the SELECT: 10 rows per workspace with the values stated, and none for RECORD_SHARING, PREBUILT_MODE, WORKFLOW_CORE_INDEX_PAGE or WEBHOOK_RATE_LIMIT. isFeatureEnabled returns !!map[key], so a missing row reads as false. This matches DEFAULT_SEEDED_FEATURE_FLAGS in seed-feature-flags.util.ts.

verdicts.correctedClaim: Lab updateLabPublicFeatureFlag accepts public flags only (WORKSPACE permission; API keys allowed). Admin-panel updateWorkspaceFeatureFlag needs a user session, SECURITY permission and canAccessFullAdminPanel. IS_FEATURE_FLAG_MANAGEMENT_ENABLED/dev/billing only control whether the UI tab shows; no CLI command exists.
verdicts.reason: IS_FEATURE_FLAG_MANAGEMENT_ENABLED is read only in client-config.service.ts (canManageFeatureFlags), and that value is consumed only by the front end. The server mutation never checks it. The class-level guards add a SECURITY settings-permission check and reject API keys. The Lab resolver accepts apiKey, oauthClient and application principals.

I opened every cited line and each label is verbatim: skills-and-agents.mdx:7, front-components.mdx:10 and :796, messaging-channels.mdx:12, timeline-activity-types.mdx:10, sync-and-recovery.mdx:101, credits.mdx:8. user-guide/ai has only an API-key safety Warning (mcp.mdx:67), no maturity label. Workflow-page labels exist that the finding does not list (see missed).
LICENSE lines 3-4 and the Commercial License near line 732 contain the production-use, Enterprise subscription for hosts and seats, and development/testing exemption wording as quoted.

LICENSE item 2 lists twenty-sdk, twenty-client-sdk, create-twenty-app, twenty-shared, twenty-ui and packages/twenty-apps as MIT. The package.json files say MIT (twenty-shared has no version field). The Twenty Application Exception definitions, permission, bundling and limits (modified Twenty stays AGPL) match.

I re-ran the grep: 458 total = 398 server, 55 front, 5 shared. verdicts.correctedClaim: isValid() only checks for a signed, unexpired validity token (from core.appToken or ENTERPRISE_VALIDITY_TOKEN); ENTERPRISE_KEY is used to fetch or refresh it. Without one, server-enforced: SSO, RLS predicate API, audit logs, a sixth workspace, custom AI providers above 25 seats. The AI usage tab is front-end only.
verdicts.reason: isValid() returns hasValidEnterpriseValidityToken() and does not read the key payload. getUsageAnalytics on the server has only AuthPrincipalGuard + SettingsPermissionGuard(WORKSPACE), with no enterprise check, so the AI-usage gate is display-only. The other gates were verified: EnterpriseFeaturesEnabledGuard on SsoResolver, hasRowLevelPermissionFeature, the event-log isValid check, and MAX_WORKSPACES_WITHOUT_ENTERPRISE_KEY = 5.

Re-checked: client-config shows isBillingEnabled False, isClickHouseConfigured False, canManageFeatureFlags True, aiModels 0. Distinct active users = 1005, and getBillableSeatCount uses the same query. The .env ENTERPRISE line is commented out. keyValuePair holds only SERVER_ID and agent-history-storage-v1 (x2), and appToken has no EnterpriseValidityToken rows (REFRESH_TOKEN count is now 2). Fetched the GitHub release pages. v2.40.0 (15 Sep), v2.41.0 (17 Sep), v2.43.0 (28 Sep) and v2.44.0 (1 Oct) each have a Breaking changes section. v2.44.0 lists agent-step conversations, agent step pausing on a question, and manifest-only registration variables. twenty/v2.42.0 (23 Sep) is a bare tag page.

Commands exist as cited: 2-40 sync-record-share-object and core-workflow-id backfills; 2-41/2-42/2-43 core workflow pointers; 2-42 migrate-agent-history-to-workspace; 2-43 enable-common-record-sharing, with the quoted comment at line 92; 2-44 verify-common-record-sharing and move-agent-chat-threads-to-record-model. rollout.md keeps the core index page behind the flag. SQL shows core.workflow and core.workflowVersion.

Manifest type at manifestType.ts:35 matches the listed arrays (it also has publicAssets and translations). MANIFEST_ENTITY_REGISTRY maps workflow, workflowVersion, validationRule, webhook, rolePermissionFlag, applicationVariable and searchFieldMetadata to NO_MANIFEST_CANDIDATES. canManifestExpressFlatEntity excludes webhook.

LogicFunctionManifest has exactly the six trigger settings. ApplicationManifest has pre/post-install, uninstall and health-check logic function hooks. RouteTriggerController is mounted on ApiPath.RouteTrigger = 's'. Caveat: LOGIC_FUNCTION_LEGACY_ROUTE_CUTOFF can move new HTTP functions to the isolated public domain when PUBLIC_DOMAIN_URL is set.

WorkflowActionType has 20 values. The factory switch throws the quoted error on its default branch. The LOGIC_FUNCTION action returns only result or error. pendingEvent: true appears only in the form, delay and ai-agent actions. WorkflowTriggerType = DATABASE_EVENT, MANUAL, CRON, WEBHOOK.

ToolCategory has 10 values. The TOOL_PROVIDERS factory is a fixed list of 10 providers. LogicFunctionToolProvider includes functions with toolTriggerSettings that pass canCallerReachApplication, names them app_<slug> and tags them LOGIC_FUNCTION. MCP direct mode lists all registry categories.

verdicts.correctedClaim: Workflow Agent steps preload only DATABASE_CRUD and ACTION registry tools. runAgent gets lazy learn_tools/execute_tool over DATABASE_CRUD, ACTION, DASHBOARD, WORKFLOW; both get none if the agent has no role. Model-native web search and twitter search are bound per modelConfiguration. No LOGIC_FUNCTION tools or load_skills.
verdicts.reason: The core claim holds. It omits that native tools include twitterSearch as well as webSearch, both opt-in per agent modelConfiguration, and that registry tools are bound only when the agent has a role.

PAUSING_TOOLS maps ask_questions, propose_email and request_form. The workflow AI agent action passes them only when isAskingQuestionsAllowed. agent-run.service passes no pausingTools (default {}). The ToolCallAnswerResolver guard has apiKey: false and requires a user for oauth/application principals.

AI_SDK_PACKAGES lists the nine packages. sdk-provider-factory switches over them and throws 'Unsupported SDK package'. ai-providers.json has six catalog providers whose apiKey templates are OPENAI, ANTHROPIC, GOOGLE, MISTRAL, XAI and TYPESAFE_AI _API_KEY. Custom entries come from AI_PROVIDERS or admin-panel addAiProvider, both subject to the seat gate.

verdicts.correctedClaim: PermissionFlagType is a closed 26-value enum; apps add flags via definePermissionFlag ('settings' or 'tool'). APPLICATION writability allows writes only from system context, or a user or application auth context whose application is the owning app, not strictly its logic functions.
verdicts.reason: isOwningApplicationAuthContext accepts user auth contexts that carry application === owning app, as well as application contexts, so the restriction is per owning-app principal. The docs' 'only your app's own logic functions' is a simplification. The 26-flag count and the manifest flag type were verified.

The docs list four locations and four ways to surface a component. WidgetType has 26 values including FRONT_COMPONENT. PageLayoutType is a closed 5-value enum. TimelineActivityTypeManifest and ToolTriggerSettings both carry frontComponentUniversalIdentifier.

STANDARD_OBJECTS has 40 top-level keys. DatabaseEventAction has six values. findLogicFunctionsTriggeredByEventName matches the four wildcard patterns quoted. Webhook is in METADATA_NAMES_WITHOUT_MANIFEST_REPRESENTATION.

AgentEntity.evaluationInputs exists; AgentManifest has no such field. evaluateAgentTurn(turnId) and runEvaluationInput(agentId, input) are on AgentTurnResolver, with AI_SETTINGS permission; runEvaluationInput rejects API keys. The grader uses getDefaultModelForTier('fast') and a hard-coded rubric prompt. I found no grader extension point.

missed.claim: Real (non-seeded) workspaces get IS_REST_METADATA_API_NEW_FORMAT_DIRECT and IS_EXECUTION_QUOTA_ENABLED switched on at activation. The seeded dev workspaces lack IS_REST_METADATA_API_NEW_FORMAT_DIRECT, so the local metadata REST format can differ from a freshly created self-hosted workspace.

The server never checks IS_FEATURE_FLAG_MANAGEMENT_ENABLED; it only feeds canManageFeatureFlags in client-config, which hides or shows the admin-panel Feature Flags tab. Any full admin with SECURITY permission can call updateWorkspaceFeatureFlag on /admin-panel in production.

Record sharing is Enterprise-licensed code with no runtime gate. The RECORD_SHARING billing entitlement and IS_RECORD_SHARING_ENABLED flag are read only by the 2-43 upgrade command, to preserve historical access. Without a key, record sharing is restricted by the license, not by the software.
missed.evidenceQuote: // This reads the former entitlement only to preserve historical access; // neither the new sharing API nor record authorization depends on it.

missed.claim: The getUsageAnalytics query has no enterprise-key check on the server: it needs only the WORKSPACE settings permission, plus ClickHouse for data. The enterprise gate for AI usage exists only in the front-end SettingsAiUsageTab.

LICENSE declares twenty-shared MIT, yet five twenty-shared files (the RowLevelPermissionPredicate* types) carry the Enterprise header. By LICENSE rule 1 those files fall under the commercial license even inside the MIT package that apps depend on.

testPlanIssues: Plan 'Where an app-defined tool is visible', step 3: getToolIndex does not work with an API key. The resolver resolves roles through userRoleService.getRoleIdForUserWorkspace(userWorkspaceId), and that throws when there is no user workspace. Fix: call getToolIndex with a user access token only, and use the API key only for the MCP tools/list check.

Plan 'Baseline', step 4 expected output: the keyValuePair query returns three rows (agent-history-storage-v1 twice, plus SERVER_ID), not two distinct keys. The enterprise validity token would be stored in core.appToken as type EnterpriseValidityToken, not in keyValuePair. Fix: expect 3 rows, and check the appToken type list for the absence of EnterpriseValidityToken. The REFRESH_TOKEN count is currently 2 and will vary.

Plan 'Turn an internal feature flag on', expected section: updateWorkspaceFeatureFlag is enforced by the user session, SettingsPermissionGuard(SECURITY) and canAccessFullAdminPanel, not by IS_FEATURE_FLAG_MANAGEMENT_ENABLED. Fix: add a check that the mutation is rejected with an API key and that the tab visibility comes from client-config canManageFeatureFlags. tim@apple.dev has canAccessFullAdminPanel = t, verified by SQL.

Plan 'Row-level permissions', step 2 expected message: the server string is 'Row level permission predicate feature is disabled.' (with a trailing period). The input fields roleId, objectMetadataId, predicates and predicateGroups are confirmed by introspection.

Plan 'Custom AI provider seat gate', expected: 'addAiProvider would be rejected with ENTERPRISE_SEAT_THRESHOLD_EXCEEDED' is correct (admin-panel-ai-provider.service.ts). But CustomAiProviderAccessService starts with hasAccess = true until its first seat count, so model resolution on a freshly started process may briefly include custom providers. Run getCustomAiProviderAccess first, which recomputes the verdict, before checking model lists.
